solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lout spreads dirt on shell from Zhengzhou cannon

indicators.note: a shell is the outside casing, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the Chinese city

indicators.note: to spread something is to push it apart, so one word splits another open and sits inside it

parts.note: muck is filth or dirt
a lout is a rude, oafish person

explanation.surface: A thug smears grime over an artillery shell made in a Chinese city.
explanation.walkthrough: The lout splits the dirt after its first letter, and the casing of Zhengzhou sits on the front. 'On' joins the two halves in an across entry: the shell goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A zumbooruck is a small swivel gun once mounted on a camel's back, so it is a kind of light artillery piece.

clue.text: Most of select group see question exchanged in a remarkable way

indicators.note: things exchanged swap places, so the two short pieces trade positions
most but not all means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a unit is a select group, as in a military unit; its last letter goes
a see is a bishop's diocese; Ely is the crossword's favourite one
QU is a standard abbreviation for question

explanation.surface: Most of an elite team being asked the same thing in turn, each in a striking manner.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names the see before the question, so the exchange is what puts them in answer order. Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done uniquely is done in a manner nobody else matches, which is a remarkable, one-of-a-kind way.

clue.text: One's meant to support bosom pal in South Africa

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an undergarment designed to hold up the breasts
second meaning: a South African slang word for a friend or mate

explanation.surface: Someone whose role is to stand by a close friend in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bosom pal' reads as one phrase meaning close friend, but the clue splits between 'bosom' and 'pal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The same three letters name the supporting undergarment and, in South African township slang, a brother or mate.

clue.text: Gold French sea shell

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A golden seashell picked up on a French beach.
explanation.walkthrough: OR for gold is heraldic, from the French word.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is an abalone, an edible Channel Islands mollusc with an ear-shaped, mother-of-pearl shell.

clue.text: Open up about families after name's put forward

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other
putting a name forward moves its abbreviation from the back of its word to the front

parts.note: clans are extended families
taken as written

explanation.surface: Make public the details of family groups once a candidate's name has been nominated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open up' looks like the definition, but 'up' is wordplay. N is the abbreviation for name, and it already sits at the end of the families word, waiting to be moved.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclasp is to release a fastening, so a clasped bag or hand is thereby opened.

clue.text: Swiss artist hosting politician, king, queen and conductor

indicators.note: a host takes a guest in, so one word holds another inside

parts.note: Paul Klee was a Swiss-born painter
Member of Parliament
R for rex, Latin for king
Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A Swiss painter entertains an MP and royalty, plus an orchestra's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The politician goes inside KLEE before its last letter, then king and queen follow. 'Conductor' wants to sit in the list of guests; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto Klemperer was a celebrated German conductor, famous for his Beethoven and Mahler recordings.

clue.text: Bard's crown among returned belongings

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters read backwards
among means in the midst of, so the letters are found inside the following word

parts.note: four letters run consecutively near the start of this word

explanation.surface: A playwright's crown found among possessions handed back.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bard is Shakespeare, so the definition is a word he used. Crown means top of the head here, not a royal headdress.
explanation.definitionFit: Nole, or noll, is an old word for the head or its crown, used by Shakespeare in A Midsummer Night's Dream.

clue.text: Far from tight, a couple of presents given beforehand

indicators.note: what is given beforehand comes earlier, so these pieces are placed ahead of the other

parts.note: two senses of present: the present time and the present place
near can mean stingy or tight-fisted

explanation.surface: Far from stingy, someone hands over two gifts early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Presents' suggests gifts, but these are the present in time, NOW, and in space, HERE. Near meaning mean with money is an old sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Nowhere near means not at all close to, so a thing nowhere near a goal is a long way off it.

clue.text: Prison wing maybe unserviceable

parts.note: a wing is an example of a limb, flagged by 'maybe'
US is the abbreviation for unserviceable

explanation.surface: A jail block that may be out of use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prison wing' reads as one phrase, but the clue breaks between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Limbus is a variant of limbo, which also has the general sense of confinement or a place of imprisonment.

clue.text: Shrew repeatedly snubbed by mice contaminated with pathogens in bloodstream

indicators.note: to snub is to cut short, and doing it repeatedly docks more than one letter from the end

parts.note: a virago is a shrew, a scolding woman; its last two letters are cut

indicators.note: contaminated things are messed up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then mixed

explanation.surface: A small mammal keeps being ignored by mice carrying disease in their blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrew' suggests the small mammal, alongside the mice, but it is the old word for a nagging woman. Snubbing twice takes off the GO.
explanation.definitionFit: Viraemic describes having viruses present in the blood, the adjective from viraemia, a kind of infection carried in circulation.

clue.text: Contain bachelor pursuing cycling ladies

indicators.note: one who pursues comes behind, so this piece is placed after the other
to cycle is to go round, so letters from the front of the word come round to the back

parts.note: ladies are women
B is the abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: Keep in check a single man who chases women on bicycles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cycling ladies' paints women on bikes, but the word tells you to rotate the letters: the last two move to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To enwomb is to hold something as if within a womb, an old poetic verb for enclosing or containing.

clue.text: One stinking hot season going topless

indicators.note: topless means with the top removed, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
summer is a season; the first letter is removed

explanation.surface: Someone who reeks in the heat of the summer months, stripped to the waist.
explanation.walkthrough: To hum is British slang for to smell bad, so a hummer is something that stinks; 'stinking hot' first reads as a phrase about the weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Hum is slang for giving off a strong smell, so one that hums is a smelly person or thing.

clue.text: Silence over Universal avoiding obscene interpretation of "category-seven" knife game in America

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed over another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'

indicators.note: to avoid something is to stay out of its way, so that letter is left out

parts.note: blue means smutty, as in a blue film
U is the British film certificate for Universal, suitable for all; this letter is taken out
category read as type, and seven as the seventh letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet about a film company's dirty reading of a hurricane rating, alongside a knife game in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Universal looks like the film studio but is the certificate letter. The quoted 'category-seven' is decoded word by word, the number becoming the letter in that position.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumblety-peg is a traditional American game in which players flip or throw a pocketknife so that its blade sticks in the ground.

clue.text: Exist without being held in positive embrace

parts.note: I am means I exist

indicators.note: what is held in something is gripped inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: plus means positive, as a plus sign
ex means without, as in ex dividend

explanation.surface: Living without ever being hugged warmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like a statement of lack but it supplies letters: EX, as in a share sold ex dividend.
explanation.definitionFit: Amplexus is the mating clasp of frogs and toads, the male gripping the female; a zoological term for that embrace.

clue.text: Keith's rubbish seafood pie full of stuff including traces of human remains

indicators.note: something full of a filling has it inside, so one piece is packed into the middle
to include is to take in, so further letters are placed inside

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish
to jam is to stuff or cram
taken as written

indicators.note: a trace is the faint first sign of something, so only first letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A dreadful clam pie found to contain bits of a body.
explanation.walkthrough: Keith is a town in Moray, so 'Keith's' marks a Scots word. The jam sits between seafood and pie, and the traces go inside the pie itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Clamjamphrie is a Scottish word for rubbish or worthless odds and ends, also used of riff-raff.

clue.text: Aide ran works with account put on tick?

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece put on another sits above it, so it is read first

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account

indicators.note: to work something is to knead and reshape it, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, then reworked

explanation.surface: An assistant ran some jobs and put the cost on credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' means on credit, but tick is the definition: the parasite, not the payment. The question mark shows a tick is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An acaridean is a member of the order of mites and ticks, so a tick is one example of it.

clue.text: Clash exposed companies plugging runners on heroin

indicators.note: exposed means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters come off
in a down entry, what is on something sits above it, so it is read first
a plug fills a hole, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: skis are runners on snow
firms are companies; the outer letters are stripped
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A scandal reveals that businesses are lending money to drug runners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runners' suggests drug couriers, given the heroin, but these runners are skis.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmish is a short, minor fight, a small-scale clash between troops or rivals.

clue.text: US Marines succeeded following panic securing European front

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so this letter is placed at the end
to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: in a lather means in a state of agitation or panic
E is the abbreviation for European
neck means cheek or nerve, as does front
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in family trees

explanation.surface: American Marines won through after alarm by capturing a European battlefront.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European front' looks like a military front line, but the two words split: one letter for the European, and front means brass neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Leatherneck is a nickname for a US Marine, from the leather collar once worn as part of the uniform.

clue.text: Once-massive French novelist's seen round English university in separate locations

indicators.note: something seen round others encircles them, so they sit inside it
separate locations means the inserted letters do not go in together but into different gaps

parts.note: Victor Hugo, author of Les Misérables, with the possessive S
E is the abbreviation for English
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A once-huge French author is spotted around an English university in different places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In separate locations' tells you the two letters go into different gaps, one each side of the O, rather than together.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugeous is an archaic or jocular word for huge, so 'once-massive' flags an old-fashioned synonym.

clue.text: Scowl about extremely arrogant French painter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to lour is to frown or scowl

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Frowning at a very arrogant French artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely arrogant' reads as very arrogant; it means the ends of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges de La Tour was a seventeenth-century French painter known for candlelit scenes, so he is one example.

clue.text: Insulate doodah's upper chamber?

parts.note: to lag pipes is to insulate them
a doodah is a thingummy, a thing whose name escapes you

explanation.surface: Lagging a gadget's top compartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper chamber' sounds like a loft or attic to insulate; it is a house of parliament. The question mark admits the term was historical.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lagting was the upper division of Norway's parliament, the Storting, so it served as a legislative second house.

clue.text: Cook stuck with electrical discharge's large disparity

indicators.note: something stuck with an item has it pushed into it, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: to fry is to cook
an arc is a luminous electrical discharge between electrodes

explanation.surface: A chef with an electric shock shows a big difference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a person, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A far cry is an idiom for something very different, so it names a wide gap between two things.

clue.text: Mud aficionado bolstered by success

indicators.note: what is bolstered has support underneath it, so in a down entry the support sits below

parts.note: an aficionado is a fan
a go can mean a success, as in 'make a go of it'

explanation.surface: Mud enthusiast encouraged by doing well.
explanation.walkthrough: A go as a success is the sense in 'make a go of it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fango is clay or mud from thermal springs, used in spa treatments, the Italian word for mud.

clue.text: Bird guano lying around weed beds

indicators.note: to bed something is to lay it in place, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: to hoe is to weed

indicators.note: something lying around has been turned about, so its letters read backwards

parts.note: guano is bird droppings, a childish word for which is poo

explanation.surface: Bird droppings scattered about where flower beds have been weeded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed beds' reads as garden beds full of weeds, but beds is a verb: the weeding tool holds the droppings.
explanation.definitionFit: The hoopoe is a crested bird with barred black-and-white wings, found across Europe, Africa and Asia.

clue.text: Drinking heavily down under, this Republican stops relating to Kiwis?

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this letter goes into the middle of the other piece

parts.note: Australian slang: to be on it is to be on a drinking binge
hic is Latin for this
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican puts a stop to heavy boozing in Australia, something concerning New Zealanders.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiwis look like New Zealanders, which fits the Australian surface; the question mark says they are the birds. 'This' gives Latin HIC, not the hiccup of a drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornithic means relating to birds, and the kiwi is a flightless bird, so the definition works by example.

clue.text: Char most of wood

indicators.note: most but not all means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: teak is a hardwood; its last letter goes

explanation.surface: Burning the greater part of the timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Char' looks like the verb to scorch, which suits the wood; it is British slang for a cup of tea, from the Chinese.
explanation.definitionFit: Char, or cha, is informal British slang for the drink made from steeping leaves, so it is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Jimmy's pointed tool's run part way through John

indicators.note: to go part way through something is to sit inside it, so one piece lands within the other

parts.note: john and bog are both slang for a toilet
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's sharp tool has gone halfway through a man called John.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy is a nickname for a Scotsman, so 'Jimmy's' flags a Scots word. John is a toilet, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Brog is a Scots word for an awl or bradawl, a pointed tool for boring small holes.

clue.text: Checking route, boy returning trifle shows fear of going back home

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: to check something is to halt it in its tracks, so one piece blocks the other by surrounding it

parts.note: to toy with something is to trifle with it
a path is a route

explanation.surface: Checking the way, a lad heading back with a small present is afraid to go home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trifle' suggests the dessert or a small gift; here it is the plaything, and it stops the route by wrapping it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostopathy is a morbid dread of returning to familiar places, from Greek nostos, a homecoming, plus pathos, suffering.
